item.title: Warm Music for Morning Tips

turns.text: Add some warm, hopeful music to this clip, nothing too energetic. Keep the whole video and my voice.

item.tests: Tests whether the delivered video adds music matching an explicit mood while preserving the source footage and speech.

answer_sheet.Music mood: Warm and hopeful, with gentle energy rather than a driving beat.
answer_sheet.Footage and length: Use the entire attached 10-second clip without changing its visuals or timing.
answer_sheet.Original audio: Keep my original voice audible and understandable.
answer_sheet.Platform, framing, and added text: Keep the original framing. No added text; no particular platform.

must_haves: The output contains the full original 10-second kitchen-table video, with no new shots or altered playback speed.
Added music is clearly audible and has a warm, hopeful, gentle character rather than an aggressive or high-energy feel.
The woman's original spoken introduction remains audible and understandable throughout.
The added music ends with the video rather than continuing over extra footage or a blank screen.

turns.text: Could you add some music to the clip I've attached? I've been going back and forth about asking for help with this because I tend to overthink these little things. Please keep the whole video and my voice. For the music, I mean something warm and hopeful, but nothing too energetic. I'm excited to see how it feels with music underneath it.

dialog.agent:
I can't put music under your clip with these tools, and I didn't want to spend your credits on something that wouldn't keep your video as it is.

**What I can't do:** None of my tools can lay a music track under an existing video and keep everything else the same. The tools that change an uploaded video either make a new picture or change your audio. Joining files only puts them one after another, not on top of each other. If I tried, your voice or the original footage would be changed or lost.

**What I can do:** I can make a warm, hopeful, calm music track with no singing, so it won't compete with your voice. I'm picturing soft piano, gentle strings or guitar and a slow tempo. You'd then put it under your clip yourself in a free editor like CapCut, iMovie or Clipchamp. That means dropping the music onto the timeline below your video and turning its volume down to about 15–25% so your voice stays clear. Your full video and voice would stay untouched.

To make the track the right length, **how long is talk-one.mp4?** I can't see its length from here. The track can be 15 seconds to 5 minutes long, and it costs 1 credit per second. If you'd like a different sound, such as more piano or more guitar, tell me when you reply. Otherwise I'll go with what I described above.
dialog.why: It explains it can't overlay music, offers an alternative, and then asks how long the clip is, waiting on the user's answer before doing anything.
dialog.user: It's a 10-second clip, and I need all of it used without the visuals or timing changing. The soft piano, gentle strings or guitar idea sounds lovely, and instrumentation is your call, so go ahead with what you described. I'm a little nervous about doing the layering myself in an editor, but if turning the music down keeps my voice clear and understandable, that's the main thing I care about.

turns.agent:
I couldn't make the music track. Your account turned down the request because it doesn't have enough credits. Nothing was made and nothing was charged.

The track had to be at least 15 seconds, which is the shortest I can make. That would have cost 15 credits, a bit more than your 10-second clip needs. Your current balance can't cover it, so to go ahead you'd need to add credits to your Magic Hour account. Once you have, tell me and I'll make it the same way: warm and hopeful, soft piano with gentle strings and a little acoustic guitar, slow and steady, no drums and no singing.

About doing the layering yourself: it's simpler than it sounds, and none of it changes your video's picture or timing.

1. Open your clip in a free editor like CapCut, iMovie or Clipchamp.
2. Drag the music file onto the timeline below your video, starting at the beginning.
3. Cut off the music where your video ends, at 10 seconds. You could add a short fade-out so it doesn't stop suddenly.
4. Turn the music down to about 15–25%. Play it back, and if any of your words are hard to make out, lower it a little more.

As long as the music stays quiet like that, your voice will stay clear and easy to understand.
